Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http: //www.dilg.com.ph DILG OPINION No. 135 s. 2022 October 20, 2022 HON. VICTOR F. BERNAL Sangguniang Panlalawigan Member, District II Province of Surigao del Norte Dear SP Member Bernal: This has reference to your letter dated 30 July 2022 seeking legal opinion from this Department on the following: I. Whether or not the Sangguniang Panlalawigan Resolution No. 147 which was passed on June 15, 2022 in the dwindling days of the past administration authorizing its outgoing governor to donate service vehicles to his favorite LGUs, Barangays and offices while clearly depriving the various departments including the office of the incoming governor, of the valuable use of these vehicles, was valid and proper; 2. Whether or not there was grave abuse of authority and grave misconduct on the part of the voting sangguniang members and of the outgoing provincial governor whose final official but questionable acts caused the midnight donations of the mentioned service vehicles, to the obvious prejudice of public service. Per your representation, Hon. Robert Lyndon S. Barbers was proclaimed by the COMELEC as the duly elected Provincial Governor of the province of Surigao del Norte as the result of the May 9, 2022 synchronized national and local elections, defeating then former Governor Francisco T. Matugas. However, the allies of the former governor in the sangguniang panlalawigan of both Districts I and II hastily issued Resolution No. 147, Series of 2022, authorizing the former governor an omnibus authority to donate the service vehicles and motorcycles of the province to component cities, municipalities and barangays before ending his term. You alleged that the subject Resolution was a clever design to paralyze the operation Of the new provincial administration. You also alleged that the Resolution hastily authorized the donation of the official vehicle of the Office of the Governor, a Kia Carnaval and a Toyota Hi-Ace Super Grandia to the Municipality of General Luna where the former Governor's wife, Sol F. Matugas is the duly elected Municipal Mayor. Also, you mentioned that ten other motor vehicles were allowed to be donated to the various municipalities and barangays in the province favored by the former Governor. Hence, the queries. I'MatIno, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

As to the first query, please be apprised that this Department, in its previous legal opinions, has been consistent that inasmuch as the resolution has undergone the procedural process for its enactment pursuant to R.A. 7160, otherwise known as the Local Government Code of 1991, the same is considered valid unless declared otherwise by proper tribunals. Accordingly, this Department is bereft of authority to rule on the legality of the subject resolution in question as this is within the jurisdiction of the regular courts. Moreover, pursuant to this Department's Memorandum Order No. 2010- 02 dated 17 September 2022, we are precluded from rendering legal opinions on those presumptively valid acts; e.g. enacted ordinance, consummated acts that already enjoy the presumption of regularity on the part of the public officer concerned, and similar instances. Thus, any issues concerning the legality or validity of a Resolution shall be threshed out by filing a special civil action for declaratory relief before the proper court in accordance with Section 1, Rule 63 of the Revised Rules of Court, which provides and we-quote: "Section I. Who may file petition. — Any person interested under a deed, will, contract or other written instrument, or whose rights are affected by a statute, executive order or regulation, ordinance, or any other governmental regulation may, before breach or violation thereof bring an action in the appropriate Regional Trial Court to determine any question of construction or validity arising, and for a declaration of his rights or duties, thereunder. " Notwithstanding, for purposes of academic discussion with the end view of guiding the parties concerned on the proper courses of action to take under the circumstances, may we provide the following provisions of law which we find applicable in the case at hand. Sections 22 and 465 of the LGC allows the Local Chief Executive (LCE) to enter into agreements, contracts or donation before the end of the term of office, thus: "SECTION 22. Corporate Powers. — (a) Every local govemment unit, as a corporation, shall have the following powers: Xxx (4) To acquire and convey real or personal property; (5) To enter into contracts; and (6) To exercise such other powers as are granted to corporations, subject to the limitations provided in this Code and other laws. Xxx (c) Unless otherwise provided in this Code, no contract may be entered into by the local chief executive in behalf of the local government unit without prior authorization by the sanggunian concerned: A legible copy of such contract shall be posted at a conspicuous place in the provincial capitol or the city, municipal or barangay hall. xxx "SECTION 465. The Chief Executive: Powers, Duties, Functions, and Compensation. — (a) The provincial govemor, as the chief executive of the provincial govemment, shall exercise such powers and perform such duties and functions as provided by this Code and other laws. Page 2 of 4

(b) For efficient, effective and economical governance the purpose of which is the general welfare of the province and its inhabitants pursuant to Section 16 of this Code, the provincial govemor shall. (I) Exercise general supervision and control over all programs, projects, services, and activities of the provincial govemment, and in this connection, shall: Xxx (vi) Represent the province in all its business transactions and sign in its behalf all bonds, contracts, and obligations, and such other documents upon authority of the sangguniang panlalawigan or pursuant to law or ordinance;" xxx (Emphasis and underlining ours) However, let it be emphasized that there is a guideline issued by the Commission on Audit (COA) concerning divestment or disposal of property. While it is true that LGUs are allowed to dispose/divest properties, COA Circular No. 89-2961 finds application, and should be strictly observed. One of the modes for the disposal/divestment of property is transfer to other government agencies. Item V (4) of the said Circular provides: "4. Transfer to Other Government Agencies Where the property or assets involved are no longer serviceable or needed by the department, agency, corporation or local government unit concerned, they may be transferred to other govemment entities/agencies without cost_or at an appraised value upon authority of the head of goveming body of the said agency or corporation, and upon due accomplishment of an Invoice and Receipt of Property." (Emphasis and underlining ours) Further, Item VI (B) and (C) states: "B. When property of a local government unit has become inserviceable for any cause, or is no longer needed, it shall, upon application of the officer accountable therefor, be inspected and appraised by the provincial or city auditor or his duly authorized representative or that of this Commission. C. The Auditor of a department, bureau or agency of the national govemment or any local govemment unit upon receipt from the department/agency head or local chief executive concemed of the Inventory and Inspection Report supported by individual equipment survey reports and current photographs, as well as the Waste Material Report, in case of waste materials and wom-out and obsolete spare parts, shall refer these documents to a Technical Property Inspector assigned to his office, if any, or to the TSO in the COA Central Office for inspection and appraisal of the 1 Entitled, "AUDIT GUIDELINES ON THE DIVESTMENT OR DISPOSAL OF PROPERTY AND OTHER ASSETS OF NATIONAL GOVERNMENT AGENCIES AND INSTRUMENTALITIES, LOCAL GOVERNMENT UNITS AND GOVERNMENT-OWNED OR CONTROLLED CORPORATIONS AND THEIR SUBSIDIARIES" Page 3 of 4

ptoperty. The Technical Propeny Inspector thus assigned shall; a) conduct an inspection of the unsetviceable equipment or property to verify justification for disposal; b) appraise the disposable equipment or propriety; and c) prepare an Inspection Report which shall indicate the following, among others: 1 - description, quantity and specifications of the equipment or property; 2 - date of purchase; 3 - acquisition cost; 4 - physical condition; 5 - appraised value; 6 - remarks/recommendations. This Inspection Repott shall be submitted to the Auditor who shall transmit the same to the proper Disposal Committee and shall be used as basis for its decisions. " As to the second query, please be informed that this department is precluded from acting on queries which are factual and justiciable in nature pursuant to DILG Memorandum Order No. 2010-02 dated 17 September 2010. Justiciable issues as defined therein pertain to those that require adjudication by the courts of law as to who between the opposing parties have the better right or a given controversy Your query contains facts that are justiciable in nature since you alleged that there was grave abuse of authority and grave misconduct on the part of the sangguniang members and of the former provincial governor that caused the donations of the mentioned service vehicles to various municipalities and barangays in the province. Thus, any factual issues or queries that are justiciable in nature shall be threshed out by the proper tribunal. The foregoing is rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion rendered by more competent authorities and the courts. We hope to have addressed your concern accordingly. Thank you. Very truly yours, YA HORITY OF TH ECRETARY: N ICTOR R. LLAMAS rsecretary for External, Legal and Legislative Affairs SELLAJVLULLLS-LRALLDnasrwrraO/ copy FURNISHED DIR. LILIBETH A.
